title: Customer POC - data classification and legal ask notes
content:
Purpose:
Capture decisions and open questions from the 2025-02-13 customer workshop (RetailCo) on POC data handling, retention, and a lightweight DPA addendum. This is a working doc for SE + Legal + Infra to align on an approach that minimizes customer risk while keeping the POC fast to spin up.

Context / scope:
- Customer: RetailCo (large retail analytics team). POC: product-recommendation assistant using customer purchase history + catalog metadata.
- Goal: 4-week POC on Redwood Hosted API, potential Dedicated evaluation.
- Primary ask from customer: confirm what data we record, how long we hold it, how to demonstrate deletion and audit for data subjects and auditors.
- Not in scope for POC: full SOC2 evidence package, long-term contractual DPA (this doc proposes an addendum template for the POC phase only).

Key constraints from the workshop:
- No raw payment card data will be sent to Redwood. Customer will mask PII before sending where possible.
- RetailCo wants generated recommendations logged for evaluation but only for 30 days.
- Security/compliance team requires: ability to redact certain customer attributes server-side, proof of deletion, and an export of logs for a 90-day audit upon request.

Proposed data classification (POC-specific):
1) Customer Identifiers (CI): names, emails, customer_id that can directly identify a person.
   - Treatment: recommend tokenization/client-side before sending; if sent, mark as Sensitive. Retention: 7 days by default for POC (short window), unless customer explicitly requests longer.
2) Transactional Records (TR): purchase history, item_ids, timestamps, aggregated purchase counts.
   - Treatment: can be kept for model/quality analysis. Retention: 30 days default for hosted POC, 90 days for Dedicated (on-request). Aggregation encouraged.
3) Derived Features (DF): embeddings, scores, personalized vectors derived by Redwood runtime.
   - Treatment: consider as non-PII if not reversible AND if customer id is not persisted next to them. Retention: 30 days; recommend TTLed cache + automatic eviction.
4) System Logs & Telemetry (SL): request traces, latency metrics, error logs, debug artifacts.
   - Treatment: logs may contain prompts/response snippets as part of debug. For POC, redact request/response bodies by default and enable limited retention: 30 days for operational logs, 90 days for audit-grade logs on explicit customer opt-in.
5) Model Artifacts & Config (MA): model version, rollout config, quant settings.
   - Treatment: metadata only, kept for life of POC.

Technical controls recommended (Hosted API POC):
- Client-side pseudonymization: customer to hash or tokenise CI fields before sending. Provide a small helper script in SDK (python/js) for deterministic salted hashing.
- Redwood runtime options to set per-route sensitive_flag=true to disable full request recording for those routes. Use token-level logging off for sensitive routes.
- KV/prefix cache TTL: configure to 30d with automatic eviction; do not persist CI keys in cache unless masked.
- Audit log export: one-click export (S3 presigned) for customer-requested audits. For POC, retention of exported audit bundle: 7 days from creation.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit. Recommend KMS integration for keys if customer requests.

Deletion proof strategy:
1) Soft-delete marker in metadata store with tombstone timestamp.
2) Background job that physically deletes data from object store and indexes within 24 hours of tombstone.
3) For KV caches and ephemeral GPU memory, guarantee eviction within 1 hour of deletion task start.
4) Provide a signed deletion certificate (JSON blob with deletion timestamp, job id, hashes of removed objects) that Legal can verify.

Sample POC DPA addendum language (working draft):
- Retention: "For the duration of the POC, Customer Data classified as Customer Identifiers will be retained by Redwood for no longer than seven (7) days unless Customer expressly approves a longer retention in writing."
- Deletion & Proof: "Upon Customer request to delete Customer Data, Redwood will mark, purge, and commence physical removal of data. Redwood will provide a Deletion Certificate within forty-eight (48) hours of job completion."
- Audit Exports: "Redwood will generate an audit export on request (Jira ticket) and retain the generated export for seven (7) days for customer collection."
- Subprocessing: "Redwood will not transfer Customer Data to external sub-processors for the POC beyond its cloud storage providers without prior written notice."
(Flag for Legal: confirm breach notification timeline and the identity of sub-processors.)

Tradeoffs & notes for Hosted vs Dedicated for POC:
- Hosted (fast): easier to set TTLs and eviction, but customer may insist on suppression of PII at ingestion. Some Legal teams dislike any hosted retention even for 7 days.
- Dedicated (slower to stand up): better for demonstrable isolation and longer retention windows; acceptable if customer wants 90d audit logs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): not recommended for a short POC due to deployment time and infra cost.

Questions for Legal / Security (open):
- Is a 7-day retention for CI defensible contractually for RetailCo region (EU data subjects)? (JIRA: JIRA-POC-9876)
- Does the Deletion Certificate phrasing require notarization or third-party attestation for mid-enterprise audits?
- Are we okay with providing audit exports that contain pseudonymised identifiers (hashes) instead of raw PII?
- Confirm whether breach notification cadence needs to be <72 hours per GDPR/contract or we need 24-hour internal escalation for POC.

Customer workshop decisions made (accepted):
- RetailCo accepted client-side tokenization as default approach for CI. (Owner: RetailCo dev lead)
- RetailCo agreed to 30d retention for transactional data for evaluation metrics.
- RetailCo asked for a deletion demonstration during the final demo. (Owner: Asha)

Action items (owners + suggested tickets):
- Build small SDK helper for deterministic salted hashing (Owner: Liam) — JIRA-ENG-4521
- Add "sensitive_flag" metadata support to per-route config and ensure logging respects it (Owner: Ravi) — JIRA-INF-4590
- Draft POC DPA addendum for Legal review with Deletion Certificate template (Owner: Asha) — CONFLUENCE-ENG-4231 / JIRA-LEGAL-121
- Prepare deletion demo script and test dataset (Owner: Sofia) — JIRA-POC-9877

Unresolved items (for next sync):
- Exact wording and timeline for the Deletion Certificate (Legal).
- Whether telemetry snippets (stack traces that include prompt fragments) must be disabled entirely for POC, or ability to enable on per-request basis is sufficient.
- Customer acceptance of pseudonymised audit exports for auditors.

Appendix: quick suggested tenant configuration for RetailCo hosted POC:
- Route: /recommendations/v1 - config: sensitive_flag=true, log_level=errors-only, kv_cache_ttl=2592000 (30d), cache_persistence=false for CI keys.
- Audit export policy: manual export via console -> S3 presigned link, retain 7d.
- KMS: optional customer-managed key (CMK) recommended if RetailCo wants encryption key ownership.

Notes to self: keep this doc as a living capture until Legal posts final addendum. Tag the final addendum and link here. Re-run workshop with RetailCo Compliance once Legal has first draft.
